headline: Dhaka residents face double crisis of gas shortage and load shedding
summary: Residents of Mohammadpur and other areas in the capital are struggling to cook as gas lines are dry and electric stoves are rendered useless by power cuts.
details: Residents of Chan Mia Housing in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, have been without gas for nearly a month, with no clear timeline for when the supply will be restored.
Many households have purchased electric stoves as an alternative, but frequent load shedding has made these stoves unusable, leaving residents unable to cook their meals.
Affected residents, including Kazi Tahmida Afroz and Russell Das, report that food is often wasted when power cuts occur mid-cooking, adding to their financial burden.
Residents are demanding a clear schedule from Titas Gas and are calling on the government to take immediate action to resolve the crisis.
The gas shortage is not limited to Mohammadpur; severe shortages have been reported in Kalabagan, Kafrul, Kazipara, West Tejturi Bazar, and Badda.
While some areas receive a small amount of gas for brief periods, most residents in these affected areas remain without any supply throughout the day.

Affected residents, including Kazi Tahmida Afroz and Russell Das, report that food is often wasted when power cuts occur mid-cooking, adding to their financial burden.

Residents are demanding a clear schedule from Titas Gas and are calling on the government to take immediate action to resolve the crisis.

The gas shortage is not limited to Mohammadpur; severe shortages have been reported in Kalabagan, Kafrul, Kazipara, West Tejturi Bazar, and Badda.

While some areas receive a small amount of gas for brief periods, most residents in these affected areas remain without any supply throughout the day.

headline_marked: US launches [[Operation Economic Outcast to isolate Iran]] globally
headline: US launches Operation Economic Outcast to isolate Iran globally
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calls it an 'Economic D-Day,' warning that any country trading with Tehran will face secondary sanctions.
details: The United States has announced sweeping new economic restrictions aimed at completely isolating Iran from the global economy. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declared the move 'Operation Economic Outcast' during a press conference in Washington.

Bessent described the operation as an 'Economic D-Day,' comparing the effort to the Allied invasion of Normandy in WWII. The goal is to cut off every economic 'lifeline' that sustains the current Iranian administration until Tehran is left isolated.

The sanctions target five critical areas: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping. The US warns that any country or company continuing to trade with Iran, particularly in oil, will be subject to secondary sanctions.

US President Donald Trump is reportedly contacting world leaders personally to request they sever ties with Iran. Treasury Secretary Bessent noted that no one is exempt from these sanctions, including Chinese banks, though diplomatic discussions are ongoing.

Tehran has rejected the restrictions, with Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stating that the US is not in a position to limit other countries' relations with Iran. He claimed that nations trading with Tehran are ignoring US warnings.
Amidst the rising tension, Pakistan's Army Chief General Asim Munir visited Tehran on Monday, meeting with Speaker Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.
caption:
The US has declared an 'Economic D-Day' against Iran. Any nation trading with Tehran now faces secondary sanctions.

The United States has announced sweeping new economic restrictions aimed at completely isolating Iran from the global economy. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declared the move 'Operation Economic Outcast' during a press conference in Washington.

Bessent described the operation as an 'Economic D-Day,' comparing the effort to the Allied invasion of Normandy in WWII. The goal is to cut off every economic 'lifeline' that sustains the current Iranian administration until Tehran is left isolated.

The sanctions target five critical areas: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping. The US warns that any country or company continuing to trade with Iran, particularly in oil, will be subject to secondary sanctions.

US President Donald Trump is reportedly contacting world leaders personally to request they sever ties with Iran. Treasury Secretary Bessent noted that no one is exempt from these sanctions, including Chinese banks, though diplomatic discussions are ongoing.

Tehran has rejected the restrictions, with Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stating that the US is not in a position to limit other countries' relations with Iran. He claimed that nations trading with Tehran are ignoring US warnings.

Amidst the rising tension, Pakistan's Army Chief General Asim Munir visited Tehran on Monday, meeting with Speaker Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.
